quick: 1.6 mg subcutaneously twice weekly (regimen varies by indication)
Used in chronic hepatitis B; no specific adjustment defined
summary: Thymosin alpha 1 (thymalfasin) is a synthetic 28-amino-acid peptide based on a naturally occurring thymic hormone, used as an immunomodulator. Depending on the country it is used for chronic hepatitis B and C, as a vaccine adjuvant (e.g. influenza), and as adjunctive immune support in certain infections and cancers. It enhances T-lymphocyte differentiation and function and natural killer cell activity. It is NOT FDA-approved in the United States (approved/marketed in numerous other countries as Zadaxin/thymalfasin); this record is based on international product information and is generally well tolerated, with injection-site reactions being most common.
indications: Treatment of chronic hepatitis B (where approved)
Treatment of chronic hepatitis C, usually in combination with other antivirals (where approved)
Immune enhancement / vaccine adjuvant (e.g. with influenza vaccine in immunocompromised or elderly patients)
Adjunctive immunomodulation in certain malignancies and severe infections (per local approvals)

dosage.d: 1.6 mg by subcutaneous injection twice weekly (about 3-4 days apart) for the prescribed course (commonly ~6-12 months)
1.6 mg subcutaneously twice weekly for a defined period around vaccination

admin: Reconstitute the lyophilised powder with the supplied diluent immediately before use and inspect the solution
Administer by subcutaneous injection, rotating injection sites
Use promptly after reconstitution; discard unused reconstituted solution
Follow the local product information for the specific indication and course length
moa: Thymosin alpha 1 is a synthetic analogue of a thymic peptide that modulates the immune system. It promotes the maturation, differentiation and function of T lymphocytes (increasing T-helper cells and CD4/CD8 responses), augments natural killer cell activity, stimulates production of cytokines such as interferon and interleukin-2, and influences Toll-like receptor signalling on dendritic cells - collectively enhancing cell-mediated immune responses against viruses and tumour cells.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to thymosin alpha 1 or excipients
relative: Immunosuppressed transplant recipients (immune-enhancing effect could theoretically promote rejection) - use only with specialist judgement
monitor: Indication-specific markers (e.g. HBV DNA/transaminases in hepatitis B)

preg: Use is not recommended during pregnancy because there are insufficient data on safety; reserve for situations where the benefit is judged to outweigh the unknown risk.
lact: Use is not recommended during breastfeeding because of insufficient data on excretion into milk and infant safety.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is established for renal impairment.
hepatic: Thymosin alpha 1 is used in chronic hepatitis B and C and no specific dose adjustment is defined for hepatic impairment; monitor liver parameters as part of disease management.

moderate: Immunosuppressant drugs - may have opposing immunomodulatory effects
Often used intentionally with interferon/antivirals (additive/complementary antiviral effect)
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described, though alcohol should be limited in liver disease.
interactions.diagnostics: May alter immune/lymphocyte parameters; interpret immune assays in this context.

monitoring: Disease-specific response markers (e.g. HBV DNA, HBeAg, transaminases in hepatitis B)
Clinical signs of any autoimmune reaction
counsel: This medicine works by supporting your immune system; it is given as an injection under the skin
Mild redness or soreness at the injection site is common and usually settles
Complete the full prescribed course even if you feel well
Tell your doctor about any other medicines, especially those that affect the immune system
Report any rash, swelling or breathing difficulty after an injection
pk: Immunomodulatory effects develop over the course of treatment
Peak plasma concentration about 1-2 hours after subcutaneous injection
Store the lyophilised vial as directed (commonly refrigerated); reconstitute immediately before use
pearls: Not FDA-approved in the US; marketed in many countries as thymalfasin/Zadaxin - this record uses international product information
Synthetic thymic peptide immunomodulator that enhances T-cell and NK-cell function
Most-studied uses are chronic hepatitis B/C and as a vaccine adjuvant; generally very well tolerated
Main adverse effect is local injection-site reaction
Theoretical caution with autoimmune disease and in transplant recipients due to immune stimulation
missed: If a twice-weekly injection is missed, administer it as soon as remembered and then continue the regular schedule, keeping doses appropriately spaced; do not double up. Contact the prescriber if multiple doses are missed.
overdose: No specific overdose syndrome or antidote is described; the peptide has a wide margin of safety. Manage any reaction supportively and monitor.
